recipes.name: Greek Avgolemono Chicken Soup
ingredients_raw: salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Rinse chicken and remove any organs that may be inside. Place in a pot large enough for it to move around, but not too big or the broth will be watery. Add the chicken neck if that is included with your chicken.

Fill the pot with enough water to cover by about 1 inch. Cover and bring to a boil. When it boils, reduce heat to low and simmer for 45 minutes to 1 hour, skimming the fat from the top as it collects. The meat should pull from the bones easily.
Transfer the chicken to a large bowl and set aside to cool.
Add rice to the broth and season with salt and pepper. Simmer over low heat until rice is tender, about 20 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, whisk eggs and lemon juice together in a bowl. Remove chicken meat from the bones.

When rice is finished, turn off the heat. Whisk one ladle full of hot broth into the eggs slowly so the eggs do not curdle. Gradually whisk in more broth until the egg mixture is heated. Pour the hot egg mixture back into the pot, whisking briskly. The result should be a creamy, cloudy-looking soup. Season with salt, pepper, or lemon juice as needed.
Add pieces of chicken to the soup before serving or serve soup with salted chicken on the side.

raw_recipe.headline: Greek Avgolemono Chicken Soup
raw_recipe.description: This is the traditional recipe made in Greek kitchens. This makes 4 to 6 large bowls of soup, for a meal, or 6 to 8 small bowls for a first course.

video.description: Nicole shows you how to make her version of this Greek classic with added chicken, onion, and garlic, topped with fresh dill and parsley, and served with crusty bread.

review.reviewBody: This was really good and just what I was looking for. The only thing that I did differently is when I bolied my chicken I added onion powder, garlic powder and some salt. I also added just a small pinch of Oregano to the soup when I added in the salt & pepper.

When we make it we put a whole onion with about 3 whole cloves pressed into the whole onion and 1 whole carrot and sometimes a celery stick with the leaves on it, whilst the chicken is boiled. You can eat the onion and carrots later with the chicken as a side dish but we usually don’t eat the celery. I’ve got a Greek background and grow up with this soup and absolutely love it.

I think this is a good recipe that may be too heavy on the lemon for those not accustomed to Avgolemono except that which is served at some restaurants--which in my opinion can be a little light on the lemon. At our house, no part of the chicken is welcome except the breast, so I just used boneless, skinless chicken breast which I seasoned with salt and a lot of black pepper before cooking with the broth and I return it to the soup after shredding. Having a Greek spouse, I don't shy away from salt, black pepper or lemon and even serve with additional on the side. If this recipe is too lemony for you, I'd add more broth and/or more rice to tone it down.

I’ve grown up with this soup from my yiayias and my mom. We do a number of things differently if you’d like to try. 1. We prefer pasta to rice. Orzo or hilopites 2. We separate the eggs. Beat the yolks with the lemon juice (usually one lemon). Beat the whites until frothy but not meringue stiff. Fold them gently into the yolks. Keep steadily stirring gently as you ladle the hot broth into the egg mixture. 3. Slowly add the warmed egg mixture back on top of the broth. Note: if using whole chicken or parts to make your broth, cook the chicken with chicken broth, carrots, celery, onion, and seasonings. Strain when done. You can pulse the veggies in a blender and add that back to the broth. It makes for a heartier broth with a lovely orange tinge!
Delicious! I used orzo instead of rice and doubled the amount because we all like soups thick and crowded.

Excellent avgolemono! My husband LOVES it! He'd never had it before I made it using this recipe, and it's spoiled him. He's tried it elsewhere and it's nowhere near as good. My only variation is the chicken. We buy a rotisserie chicken from big-box store. After having chicken the first night, we pull almost all of the chicken off the bones and save it for leftovers. I use the bones to make stock, using mirepoix & spices. Then the next day, I heat the stock, and continue with the recipe as written. I chop some of the leftover chicken and add it back into the soup at the last minute so it doesn't dry out. Fabulous!

I used 2 large chicken breasts instead of a whole chicken. Otherwise I thought this was kind of bland. I had zested the lemons before juicing them. I ended up throwing the zest in after tasting the finished soup. It was still bland and I added some Greek seasoning that I had in my cabinet. The recipe is very easy. I cooked the chicken breasts for about 1 hr 20 min. I took them out and shredded them on a plate.
Really good. Careful with the lemon... 2 was pretty strong. Had to dilute with chicken broth and a couple more eggs. Try one, then add the second if necessary.

I made this minus the chicken, added some carrots, celery, yellow onions, garlic, jalapeno peppers, basil, oregano , rosemary, and red pepper flakes. It was okay, though the lemon was a little too strong.

I decided to try a new Avgolemono recipe and it was a mistake: This recipe wasn't sufficiently sour nor creamy. I thought the recipe looked "off" when it called for only 3 eggs and 2 lemons. 

The recipe I usually make and will go back to has (9) egg yolks and the juice of (5) lemons and it tastes just like the soup the owners of a Greek restaurant made - and they were from Greece. Customers would call to see if it was the soup of the day and hang up if we answered, "No today it's vegetable.." 

Beloved and for a reason: The egg-ier and more sour recipe is far superior to this one.

I make the soup very often. In the water, I add 2 medium carrots, celery, one zucchini if I have one,a good size onion, and one potato along with the chicken. I remove the froth as it cooks. Remove the chicken when it’s cooked clean the chicken , I removed the celery because of the fibers and blend all the remaining vegetables that remain with some broth and add it back to the broth. Salt and pepper to taste. My family loves it with orzo and once that cooks, I add the egg lemon juice which has been tempered with a hot broth that I have beaten together.
This is a great recipe that reminds me of home!!
I made half the recipe to try and it came out great. So I will be making more.
I followed Kathryn Kariotis' Yaya's method. A+++
Your the best Dimi - Galin Anastasi
So yummy! Was looking for an easy recipe, espeicaially one without cream and this was perfect. Thanks! This one will definite be becoming in rotation of my meals!
Loved it, but I've had it made by my friends yaya
I used to make it with my family all the time. Great soup when you have a cold 😁 Thanks for the recipe 😁
So perfect! Very simple, but delicious. My husband couldn't quit eating it.
I added green onions to the top and served with Rye bread! Perfect dinner!
